name: Canasta
tagline: Meld with your partner, freeze the pile, and build canastas of seven.

rulesSummary: Three players: 13 cards each; draw two, discard one. Everyone plays alone until someone takes the pile.
Whoever takes the pile first stays alone, and the other two become partners for the hand (melds joined, red 3s kept apart). Scores are kept per player.
Head to head: 15 cards each. Draw two and discard one. You need two canastas to go out.
Three pairs, partners across. Three decks and six jokers, 13 cards each. A side needs two canastas to go out.
Red 3s: 100 each, but five are 1,000 and all six 1,200.
Meld cards of one rank and build canastas of seven. Two decks and four jokers.
Each turn: draw, or take the whole discard pile by melding its top card. Then meld and discard.
Jokers and 2s are wild. A meld is 3+ cards of one rank with at least 2 naturals and at most 3 wilds. Seven cards make a canasta, squared up: 500 natural (a red card on top), 300 mixed (a black one).
Red 3s are laid out at once and replaced. Black 3s can only be melded when going out (no wilds). One on top blocks the pile for the next player.

To take the pile, meld its top card with a natural pair, or one natural and a wild, or add it to your side's meld. Frozen (a wild or a turned-up red 3 in it), or before your side has melded: you need a natural pair.
Your side's first meld must be worth 50 (90 from 1500, 120 from 3000, 15 below zero). Joker 50, 2 and A 20, K–8 10, 7–4 and black 3 5. From the pile, only its top card counts.
You need a canasta to go out: meld everything, or all but one and discard it. Out is 100, or 200 concealed (whole hand in one turn, own canasta, nothing earlier; no minimum if you drew).
With a partner, you may ask “May I go out?” after drawing, before melding from your hand. The answer binds: yes means you must (if you can), no means you can't.
When the stock runs out, play goes on while players take the discard. You must take it if it isn't frozen and matches your side's meld. A red 3 drawn last ends play.
Score melds, canasta bonuses and red 3s (100 each, 800 for all four; minus if your side hasn't melded). Cards in hand count against you. At the target (5000 unless changed), the highest score wins.
